title: On the discretization of the object space in inverse problems with application to cryo-electron microscopy
summary: In many inverse problems, the aim is to recover a probability distribution on a latent (or object state) space from indirect, noisy observations. When the observations can be modelled as noisy samples from the mixing latent distribution, the recovery problem is a deconvolution problem on the space of probability measures. A common strategy is to fix a finite set of candidate points and estimate a weight for each, turning the problem into a finite-dimensional concave maximum likelihood problem on the simplex.
